**Inverse-probability weighting compensates for unequal treatment chances by giving rare observed choices more weight.** If someone with given covariates had treatment probability 0.2, an observed treated outcome receives weight five. A comparable control receives weight 1/0.8=1.25. [1](https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook)

Under consistency, conditional exchangeability, and positivity, these weighted observations can represent a balanced target population for estimating an average effect.

**Extreme propensities make a few observations dominate.** At probability 0.001, a treated observation gets weight 1000. One unusual outcome or a small propensity-model error can then strongly change the estimate. Inspect overlap and effective sample size, not just nominal row count.

Clipping or trimming stabilizes variance but introduces bias or changes the target population. Doubly robust methods combine propensity and outcome models and can tolerate one being misspecified under other required conditions. They cannot manufacture missing counterfactual evidence when a group never receives one treatment, nor remove unmeasured confounding. State the population, assumptions, and stabilization rule with the effect estimate.

**Technical details and references.**

With $e(X)=P(T=1|X)$, inverse-probability weighting reweights treated observations by $1/e(X)$ and controls by $1/(1-e(X))$. Under consistency, conditional exchangeability, and positivity, this can identify a population average treatment effect. Near-zero or near-one propensities yield huge weights, high variance, and sensitivity to model errors. [1](https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook)

Trimming or clipping weights trades variance for bias and can change the target population; report the rule, overlap diagnostics, and effective sample size. Doubly robust estimators combine outcome and propensity models and can remain consistent when one is correctly specified, under the other identification/regularity conditions. They do not fix a genuine absence of overlap or unmeasured confounding. If treatment is never observed for a group, its missing counterfactual cannot be recovered by a clever weight alone.
